content.text: What would be the best way to allow Claude to know which Jira tickets I have in progress

Best approach: don't store the ticket list itself in memory — status changes too often and would go stale. Instead, just ask me to query Jira live via JQL (e.g. `assignee = currentUser() AND status = "In Progress"`) whenever you want a current view; the Atlassian MCP tools (`searchJiraIssuesUsingJql`, `getJiraIssue`) already appear connected in this session.

The one thing worth saving to memory is a *reference* — e.g. your Jira project key(s) or a standard JQL filter you use — so I don't have to ask "which project?" every time. Want me to save that once you tell me the project key?

Jira tickets for this project (next-www-toastboy) use project key `SYS` (e.g. SYS-558, SYS-557, SYS-556 — matches commit message prefixes seen in git log).

To check in-progress tickets, query live via the Atlassian MCP tools rather than caching a list here (status changes too often to keep in memory) — use JQL like:

```
project = SYS AND assignee = currentUser() AND status = "In Progress"
```

content.text:
Compared your diff in [AdminUserList.tsx](src/components/AdminUserList/AdminUserList.tsx) against the SYS-559 checklist, cross-referenced against how the sibling admin pages ([players/page.tsx](src/app/footy/admin/players/page.tsx), [admin/page.tsx](src/app/footy/admin/page.tsx), [AdminPlayerList.tsx](src/components/AdminPlayerList/AdminPlayerList.tsx)) already solved the same checklist items. A few gaps:

1. **"Page title and main heading are correct and consistent"** — the page's `metadata.title` is `'Users'` ([page.tsx:11](src/app/footy/admin/users/page.tsx:11)), but your new heading says **"Auth Users"** ([AdminUserList.tsx:96](src/components/AdminUserList/AdminUserList.tsx:96)). Neither matches the other, and neither follows the "Admin: X" pattern the other admin pages use (`"Admin: Players"`, `"Admin Dashboard"`).

2. **Heading placement/pattern inconsistency** — every other admin page puts the `Title` in the page component, wrapped in `<Center>`, outside the `Paper`. You've put it inside the component, inside the `Paper`, using `ta="center"` + a `Divider` instead. Not wrong, but it's a different pattern than the rest of the site for no apparent reason — worth reconsidering for consistency.

3. **"Interactive elements have adequate sizing and touch targets"** — your sortable column headers are still a raw `Table.Th` with `onClick` + `style={{ cursor: 'pointer' }}` ([AdminUserList.tsx:111](src/components/AdminUserList/AdminUserList.tsx:111)). `AdminPlayerList` solved this exact checklist item with an `UnstyledButton` (`type="button"`, `aria-label="Sort by X"`) plus `aria-sort` on the `Table.Th`. Yours has no keyboard focus, no `aria-sort`, and no real touch target — this checklist item isn't met yet.

4. **Leftover TODO comment** — line 98 has `{/* TODO: Do I want these dividers?... */}`. That's an open design question, not a finished decision — worth resolving before calling this polished (and the project convention is no comments unless the WHY is non-obvious).

5. **Untested**: "No overflow, clipping, or awkward wrapping at any viewport width" — the table has no column width constraints (unlike `AdminPlayerList`'s `tableLayout: 'fixed'` + explicit `w=` per column), so long emails/names could wrap awkwardly on mobile. Worth checking at 375px before ticking that box.

Everything else (Mantine component usage, admin action labelling via the `Switch` `aria-label`, general structure) looks consistent with the rest of the site.
